one_month_reasoning: Correction from round 1: Q3 2026 results are not scheduled inside the window. Materion has not announced a date. It has reported Q3 exactly 33 days after quarter end every year from 2022 to 2025, Q3 2026 ends Oct 2, and MarketBeat's estimate is Nov 4. Results therefore most likely come 2026-11-04, after the 1-month close on Fri 2026-10-30 (Nov 1 is a Sunday). The window holds only the date announcement (around Oct 21), peer semi/A&D prints in late October (read-through, two-sided), and the risk that the Oct 1-2 +16% move fades, since it had no filing or identified catalyst; the Jefferies initiation was already public around Sep 2. More directors sold in late Aug/early Sep at about $232-235 (InsiderTrades); that is a weak signal. So I take out the earnings jump and use a lognormal with median $309.5, a small give-back of the unexplained spike, and sigma 15.2% over about 20 trading days (59% annual / 3.5 = 16.9%, less the earnings component). This is close to symmetric. The skeptic view is about valuation and plays out over quarters, not weeks.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM P/E (2028E $9.55 x 28x = $267, 55%), NTM EV/EBITDA (2028E adj $360M x 17x less $350M net debt / 21.1M = $273, 35%) and FCF yield ($150M at 3% = $237, 10%). That gives about $266 a year out, about 15% below $312.

inputs_detail.derivation: Round 1 used my own $8.30. I now use consensus: stockanalysis $8.43 (+20.1%), MarketBeat $8.48.

+13% on 2027 consensus. That is below the +20% expected for 2027 because EPS was flat to down over 2022-2025 (GAAP $4.14, $4.58, $0.28, $3.58) and semi is 54% of net sales, so I assume mid-cycle growth.

Peer median forward P/E is 32.9x (range 14.5-39.7x; 11 peers, stockanalysis, Oct 3 2026), and MTRN today is 39.4x. 28x is a ~15% discount to the peer median and sits inside the peer range. The discount rests on three things. Next-year EPS growth is below the peers (MTRN +20% vs a ~26% peer median). EBITDA margin on net sales is about 10%, against roughly 20% for the peer median, which reflects pass-through metal and a less-differentiated mix. And FCF conversion has been chronically weak: FCF of $7-38M a year in 2022-2025 and $39M in H1 2026. See comps_summary.

bear.story: AI/semis digestion or a customer inventory correction hits Electronic Materials (54% of net sales). FY27 EPS stalls near $7.4, well under the $8.45 consensus, repeating 2022-2025's sideways EPS. The multiple falls to about 22x, the low end of specialty-materials peers, and the stock round-trips toward the July low ($189).

base.story: Consensus is met (2027 about $8.45, NTM about $9.5) but the multiple compresses from about 39x forward to about 30x as growth normalizes toward peer levels. The stock ends modestly below today.

bull.story: Backlog (+30%) and RPO ($116M) convert, defense beryllium and data-center telecom drive 2027 EPS above $9 and 2028 above $11, and the market keeps a top-of-peer-range multiple of about 38x.

thesis_break_reason: $200 is below the Aug 24 post-print low (~$230) and about 24x FY2027 consensus ($8.45). Close to the Jul 29 pre-print low of $189. A sustained trade there would mean the Q2 beat-and-raise re-rating has fully unwound, most likely because the Nov 4 or Feb guide disappointed or semi/data-center backlog fell. That would be the AI/defense growth leg failing, not ordinary 55-60% volatility. I keep $200 rather than the supervisor's $190: the July drawdown to $189 happened before the Q2 print, so it reflects pre-raise fundamentals. Revisiting it after the raise is a stronger signal.

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI/semis demand: semiconductor is 53.6% of H1 2026 net sales
Multiple compression: MTRN is 39.4x forward P/E against a 32.9x peer median, despite below-median EPS growth and margins
FCF conversion: $7-38M a year 2022-2025 and $39M in H1 2026 against adjusted EPS above $5. Q2's $58.7M has to repeat

reasoning: Round 2, skeptic lane. The supervisor confirmed my core facts: net debt $420.7M, 21.1M diluted shares, 54% semis share, the GAAP-vs-adjusted gap, weak FCF history and insider selling. It corrected three points, which I accept. (1) Q3 results are most likely 2026-11-04, outside the 1-month window. (2) FY2027 EPS consensus is about $8.45 (MarketBeat $8.48; stockanalysis now shows $8.43). I moved from my own $8.30 to consensus, which lifts 2028E from $9.30 to $9.55. (3) FCF is starting to inflect (H1 $39M, Q2 $58.7M). I cut the FCF leg's weight from 20% to 10% rather than raise its value, since one quarter does not establish a trend. On the supervisor's 'unverified +9% 2027 revenue consensus' point: stockanalysis now shows 2027 revenue $2.60B, +9.16%, so the figure stands. On double-counting de-rating: I raised EV/EBITDA from 16x to 17x and kept 28x P/E. I tested both against an 11-peer comp set of specialty alloys, A&D materials and semi materials/equipment (CRS, ATI, HWM, HXL, KALU, ENTG, ESI, MKSI, ROG, COHR, UCTT). The peer median is 32.9x forward P/E and about 21x derived forward EV/EBITDA. MTRN's next-year EPS growth (+20%) is below the peer median (~26%), its EBITDA margin on net sales (~10%) is about half the peer median, and its FCF conversion is the weakest in the group. So a persistent discount to the median is justified, and both my multiples sit inside the peer range. Today MTRN trades at a premium (39.4x), which is the skeptic's core point. Fair value rises from $253 to $266. Scenarios are $170/$290/$430 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$295). The 12-month ladder is lognormal with median $295 (up from $288) and sigma 0.50: below the 59% realized vol, which was inflated by re-rating jumps, but well above large-cap base rates. The 1-month ladder drops the earnings jump: median $309.5, sigma 15.2%. Research this round was limited: Twelve Data statistics were paywalled and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so peer data comes from stockanalysis statistics and forecast pages, and forward EV/EBITDA is derived (see comps_summary).

comps_summary.peer_median_growth_next_yr: EPS ~+26% (median of the 10 peers with a next-year figure; KALU excluded)
comps_summary.mtrn_today: Forward P/E 39.4x (stockanalysis); EV $6.99B / 2026E adj EBITDA ~$275M = ~25x (30x on stockanalysis's derived basis); FY2027 EPS growth +20.1%
comps_summary.mtrn_in_fair_value: P/E leg 28x NTM: a ~15% discount to the 32.9x peer median, inside the range. EV/EBITDA leg 17x on adjusted EBITDA (~20x on the peers' reported basis): a ~6-20% discount to the 21.3x median, inside the range.
comps_summary.justification: I hold a discount to the peer median through the horizon on four measurable grounds, and none of them is a sell-side relative call. (1) Growth: consensus FY2027 EPS growth is +20% for MTRN against a ~26% peer median, and value-added sales grew only ~15% in Q2 against +42% net sales. (2) Margins: TTM EBITDA is ~10% of net sales (stockanalysis $205M / $2.10B), against roughly 18-27% for CRS, ATI, ENTG, ESI, HXL, MKSI and HWM. Even the company's 23% target is on value-added sales, which excludes pass-through metal. (3) Cyclicality and earnings quality: GAAP EPS of $4.14, $4.58, $0.28 and $3.58 over 2022-2025, FCF never above $38M a year, and P/FCF ~312x trailing. That is the weakest cash conversion in the set, and semis (54% of net sales) is the most cyclical end market here. (4) The balance sheet is neutral: ~1.5x net leverage is in line with peers (e.g. ESI ~3.4x, ENTG ~3.5x, CRS ~0.4x), so it gives no premium and no discount. Against that, MTRN's beryllium position (sole Western integrated producer, customer-funded defense capacity) is a real moat, which is why I do not push it to the bottom of the range (KALU/UCTT/MKSI at 15-18x). The peer medians are themselves elevated by the 2026 AI/aerospace rally, so the peer-median anchor already carries some upside risk to my numbers. Caveats: forward EV/EBITDA for peers is derived, assuming constant margins, because Twelve Data statistics were paywalled and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited. KALU's growth figure is current-year because next-year is paywalled. COHR's and CRS's fiscal years end in June.
